question.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-6y=2 \\ -4x+24y=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-6y=2 \\ 0x+0y=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-2$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-2,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

evidence.solution_quote: Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

question.knowledge_point: Reducing an Augmented Matrix for a Singular 2x2 System to REF and Solving the Resulting System
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
